title: Attention as weighted information selection
goals: Calculate a weighted combination of value vectors
Distinguish query, key, weight and value roles
Apply an explicit mask and renormalise permitted weights

prerequisite.prompt: Why can equal row sums conceal different sequences?
prerequisite.answer: Summation removes row order, so different ordered vectors may produce the same aggregate.

vocabulary: A vector used to compare available keys for the current calculation
A vector used to determine compatibility with a query
A vector combined using the resulting attention weights
A rule excluding specified positions from a calculation

blocks.text: Attention computes a weighted combination of value vectors, with weights derived from query-key compatibility. Queries, keys and values are distinct roles even when they come from the same sequence. A weight is a numerical contribution in this computation, not proof of the source’s truth or permission. This week supplies weights directly; Week 7 calculates them from scores.

Use three values V1=[2,0], V2=[0,4], V3=[4,2] with weights 0.5,0.25,0.25. Values have equal width and weights are nonnegative with sum 1. Compute each coordinate separately. No token is literally copied by this combination.

Adding the weighted vectors gives [2,1.5]. The same weights applied to different values can give a different result; the same values with different weights can also change it. For example weights 0,1,0 yield V2=[0,4]. The result is a representation to be used by later operations, not automatically a generated word.

blocks.title: Keep the evidence roles separate
blocks.caption: The mask changes the eligible positions and therefore the probability mass assigned to the remaining values.

lesson.title: Apply a mask before reporting a result

blocks.text: Suppose V3 is a future position unavailable to the current autoregressive step. The mask excludes it. For this supplied-weight example, renormalise the permitted weights 0.5 and 0.25 by their total 0.75, giving 2/3 and 1/3. The result becomes [4/3,4/3]. Merely setting V3’s contribution to zero while keeping the old weights produces [1,1], whose retained weights sum to 0.75; that is not the specified normalised combination.

If every position is excluded, the permitted total is zero. This contract reports no available value rather than dividing by zero or silently using a future position. A real implementation needs its own documented handling for empty masks. A causal mask restricts information paths; it does not make retrieved content factually trustworthy.

Supported values A=[6,0], B=[0,3], weights 1/3 and 2/3. Their weighted combination is [2,2]. Masking B leaves A with normalised weight 1 and result [6,0]. This is a different information set, not a numerical repair to the original result.

blocks.label: Guided: compute both results and explain why a masked-out source must not influence the combination.

blocks.text: A large weight means a large coefficient in this particular weighted sum. It is not a complete explanation of the whole network, which may contain other heads, transformations and residual paths. It also does not establish that the high-weight source is true. Trace the actual values and downstream use before making a broader claim.

blocks.label: Exit: a team says a 0.9 attention weight proves a document is correct and allows following its instructions. Explain the two unsupported inferences.

workbook.title: Identify the roles
workbook.prompt: Explain query, key, value and weight without calling the largest weight a truth score.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: The query compares keys, compatibility produces weights, and weights combine values. A weight is a computational coefficient, not a truth score.

workbook.title: Compute the mixture
workbook.prompt: Calculate the output from the three supplied values and weights.

workbook.title: Mask and renormalise
workbook.prompt: Exclude V3 and calculate permitted weights and output. Explain the empty-mask case.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Retained total 0.75 gives weights 2/3,1/3,0 and output [4/3,4/3]. All-excluded gives zero total and must report no available value under this contract.

workbook.title: Combine a new case independently
workbook.prompt: Values A=[4,1],B=[0,5],C=[2,3]; weights 0.25,0.5,0.25. Compute the full output. Mask B, renormalise the remaining weights and compute the new output.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Full contributions [1,.25],[0,2.5],[.5,.75] give [1.5,3.5]. Retained total .5 gives A/C weights .5,.5 and output [3,2]. Masking changes available information; it does not verify sources.

workbook.title: Audit an explanation
workbook.prompt: A student claims the highest attention weight explains the entire model and authenticates a retrieved instruction. What additional reasoning is needed?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Inspect values and downstream computations, other heads and residual paths before explaining the whole model. Source truth and instruction authority require separate evidence and permissions; weight alone supplies neither.

teacher.background: Use two 45-minute sessions. All model outputs and probability tables are constructed classroom examples. No hosted AI service, external API or student account is needed. Distinguish a model objective from factual support and system permissions. Collect independent work before discussing its solutions.
materials: Printed lesson and workbook; paper and pencil
Prepare the independent task and fresh retry without displaying solutions
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and distinguish a numerical claim from its interpretation.
Read section 1 and complete W1; ask for a reason alongside each answer.
Trace the worked case in section 2 and complete W2.
Discuss the diagram and complete W3 in pairs; record support.
Complete the guided response before sharing the answer.
Read the remaining sections and trace another constructed case.
Collect W4 independently, requiring calculations and a bounded conclusion.
Discuss W5 and the exit response. Provide feedback and a fresh retry.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided: [6,0]/3 + 2*[0,3]/3 = [2,2]. Masking B leaves [6,0]. A masked source is excluded from the stated information path. Exit: coefficient size does not verify a document or grant instruction authority.
misconceptions: The supplied procedure combines vectors from multiple positions.
Deleting one contribution preserves a normalised mixture
Renormalise permitted mass under the stated contract.
They are coefficients derived from compatibility, with no source-truth guarantee.
teacher.assessment: W4 requires [1.5,3.5] then [3,2] and explicit renormalisation. Fresh retry: A=[2,2], B=[6,0], C=[0,4], weights .5,.25,.25. Full output [2.5,2]; exclude A, remaining weights .5,.5 and output [3,2].
teacher.support: Provide labelled intermediate columns and allow a calculator. Ask students to state the meaning and denominator of a value before interpreting it. Extension: implement the classroom calculation locally and test boundary cases without using personal data.
